prose.summary: Mansha cannot confirm whether the cosmetic skin creams meet the rule of origin for the CEPA rate yet, because the 6-digit HS code for the non-originating input 'Emollients' is missing. If the product meets the rule, the estimated saving would be 12000.00 AED.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 33049990, described as Other beauty or make-up preparations. Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 20% and the CEPA rate is 0%. If the product meets the rule of origin, the estimated saving is 12000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) for each non-originating input, meaning each such input must be classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the finished product, and a value addition (VA) of at least 40%, which is the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials. Because the 6-digit HS code for the non-originating input 'Emollients' is missing, the origin check cannot be completed. No checks or totals were calculated.

notes.text: The agreement refers to box 8 for the certificate remark, but India's origin rules and certificate form use box 9; since India's form governs entry into India, you should use box 9.
UAE law requires records to be kept for at least 3 years, but the CEPA requires 5 years for CEPA claims, so you must keep records for 5 years.
The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 40%' is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass), but the agreement does not define '+'; this is Mansha's interpretation.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
The agreement says box 8 for the certificate remark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this comes from secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022), not the official text.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The certificate fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED.
The certificate fee estimate assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.
